title: Football transfer rumours: Real Madrid's Luka Modric to Inter?
trail: Zinedine Zidane to replace José Mourinho? | Simon Mignolet to Napoli? | Lee Cattermole to Bordeaux? | No really, Lee Cattermole to Bordeaux?
body: Six years and 14 trophies after joining Real Madrid from Tottenham Hotspur, Luka Modric fancies a change of scenery and remains heavily linked with a move to Inter. The 32-year-old Croatian is reported to be keen on a move to Serie A and his potential new boss Luciano Spalletti had plenty to say on the matter after inking a new deal with Inter yesterday, while simultaneously saying very little. “I will not say anything more with regards to the transfer market,” the Inter boss said yesterday. “I’m already very happy with I have in my squad. These players are the ones I would want to have.” Spalletti went on to say that he is sharing a dressing room “with people I would have chosen even if I was playing a computer game”, but failed to specify if the game in question was Fortnite or the 1986 arcade classic Bubble Bobble. French sports daily L’Equipe say that Zinedine Zidane would quite like to work in England, prompting inevitable idle speculation that he will replace José Mourinho when the disaffected Portuguese manager eventually leaves Manchester United. Atlético Madrid defender Diego Godin, a United target over the summer, has revealed that he rejected the advances of several clubs but “decided to stay for personal reasons”. Danny Drinkwater’s days as a bit-part player at Chelsea look numbered after Maurizio Sarri let it be known the midfield will be allowed to leave Stamford Bridge before the August 31 European deadline. Meanwhile at the midfielder’s former club, Leicester City, English lion-heart Harry Maguire is sitting with pen poised, waiting for somebody to push a £70,000-per-week contract within signing range. Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet is expected to sign for Napoli before the Italian transfer window inches shut on Friday and the Belgian could be joined in Italy by forgotten Arsenal man, Joel Campbell, who is off to Frosinone. The Lazio-based Serie A minnows were promoted to the Italian top flight for only the second time in their history this summer. Mohamed Elneny, Carl Jenkinson and David Ospina look to be headed for the Emirates exit door after Arsenal manager Unai Emery was instructed to free up some wages following his £70m summer spending spree. Right-back Jenkinson is surplus to requirements after failing to impress on loan at Birmingham City last season, while Marseille are interested in midfielder Elneny. Colombian goalkeeper Ospina has been linked with a move to Turkish side Beşiktaş for months, but the two clubs are reported to be at an impasse over the fee. Lee Cattermole is the subject of unlikely speculation linking him with a loan move to Ligue 1, where his former boss Gus Poyet is managing Bordeaux and in need of an ageing midfield enforcer. On £40,000 per week as a League One player with Sunderland, Cattermole has three years left on his contract and the two clubs are attempting to thrash out an agreement. And finally, Brendan Rodgers’ future as Celtic manager looks less assured after the Scottish champions exited this season’s Champions League in the qualifying rounds. While calls for the Northern Irishman’s head from a pike-waving Twitter mob seem laughably premature, his apparently fractious relationship with those keeping a very tight hold of the club’s purse-strings may prompt him to seek alternative employment now that his team look destined for this season’s Europa League. Rodgers denied reports he was thinking of walking away in the build-up to last night’s defeat at the hands of AEK Athens, but may change his tune in the inevitable event of a Premier League job becoming available.
